Both candidates improperly duplicate FilesService.Add instead of routing Upload through it, but B additionally makes a broad, explicitly forbidden RawClient retry/body-ownership change.","reasons":["A preserves the existing request/retry implementation and limits production changes to FilesService.Upload and documentation.","B modifies RawClient.Do to seek, measure, rewind, and change ownership semantics for every io.ReadSeeker, directly conflicting with the contract's instruction not to refactor unrelated retry machinery.","B's GetBody closure reuses and mutates one shared seeker, adding subtle redirect, retry, and concurrency risks beyond the requested buffered-upload solution.","A provides separate validation errors for an empty filename and nil content, while B collapses both cases into a less precise error."],"risks_a":["Upload calls Raw.Do directly and duplicates Add's option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data behavior instead of routing through Add as explicitly required.","The visible tests do not cover validation or source-reader failures.","The retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than an os.File-like streamed source and does not explicitly set RetryAllMethods, so it is less faithful to the reported scenario."],"risks_b":["Upload also bypasses Add and duplicates its request path, violating the central reuse requirement.","The RawClient.Do changes are unnecessary scope expansion and alter behavior for Add, Update, Raw.Do, and all other seekable request bodies.","The shared-seeker GetBody implementation can be fragile because retries obtain bodies by repositioning the same reader rather than receiving independent readers over buffered data or a fresh source handle each time; it also introduces seek/measurement failures for previously accepted readers and changes close semantics globally under the guise of this feature fix. No current race test demonstrates safety for concurrent body use or redirects, and an unusual ReadSeeker may not support SeekEnd even though it was previously usable as an io.Reader. Wait this is all one reason? Need concise. Also source-reader failure test missing."]}
